Master of Global and Digital Public Health Leadership Frequently Asked Questions
Global & Digital Public Health Leadership Frequently Asked Questions

Welcome to our special preview of the Master in Global and Digital Public Health Leadership at Dubai Medical University. Today, we’re answering the most frequent questions from prospective students to help you decide if this is the right path for your leadership journey.
The Master in Global & Digital Public Health Leadership (MGDPHL) Leading the Future of Global Health
What makes this program special compared to other Master’s in Public Health?

What sets this program apart is its unique integration of four critical pillars: Leadership and Governance, Global Health Systems, Humanitarian Action, and Digital Public Health (including AI). Benchmarking against top international universities like Harvard and Johns Hopkins shows that no other program currently integrates all four of these specific pillars into a single Master’s degree. It is a purpose-built, interdisciplinary curriculum designed specifically to fill a critical gap in the UAE’s graduate health education landscape.
Why should I join this specific program now?

The program is explicitly aligned with major national and global initiatives, such as UAE Vision 2031 for health modernization and the National AI Strategy 2031. By joining, you are positioning yourself at the forefront of digital transformation, AI ethics, and climate-resilient health systems that are currently top priorities for health authorities and international agencies like the World Health Organization (WHO).
Am I the right candidate for this Master’s?

We are looking for the next generation of health system leaders. To be a strong candidate, you should have a Bachelor’s degree in a health-related field (such as medicine, nursing, pharmacy, or public health) with a minimum GPA of 3.0. While we prefer candidates with two years of professional experience in health or humanitarian roles, we welcome all dedicated professionals who meet the English proficiency requirements (IELTS 6.5+ or equivalent).
What exactly will I be studying?

The 30-credit hour MSc curriculum is designed in progressive stages, allowing you to build leadership, policy, humanitarian, and digital public health expertise through stackable modules and advanced applied learning.

● Semester 1 (Leadership & Systems Competencies): You will study Leadership & Change, Governance & Performance, Global Health Systems, and Policy & Global Health Diplomacy. This phase develops core competencies in leadership, governance, health systems analysis, and policy-making.

● Semester 2 (Health Security, AI & Innovation): You will focus on Global Health Security, Humanitarian Systems & IHR, Disaster Medicine & Emergency Preparedness, Digital & AI-Enabled Public Health Systems, and AI Ethics, Governance & Cyber Resilience in Health.

● Semester 3 (Specialization, Practice & Research): You will choose one of two advanced tracks: Health Systems & Policy Track or Digital Health & Global Leadership Track. You will also complete an Applied Internship in AI & Digital Public Health Leadership and a Thesis, enabling you to apply learning to real-world challenges and produce evidence-based solutions.
What is the teaching method? Will I just be sitting in lectures?

Not at all. The program uses a blended delivery mode, combining online learning with on-campus (evening and weekends) blocks. We emphasize active and experiential learning. You will participate in simulation exercises for pandemics and humanitarian crises, policy labs where you debate real-world data, and design thinking sprints to prototype health innovations.
What are the potential career opportunities after I finish?
The program is designed to meet a verified "workforce gap". Graduates will be equipped to take on leadership roles in:
International health agencies (WHO, UN agencies, TGF, GAVI, World Bank, etc).
Digital health and AI governance sectors, where there is a high demand for leaders who can govern complex ethical and technical systems.
What are the requirements for graduation?

The program is designed with a flexible stackable pathway to suit working professionals and different study schedules. You may complete the full 30-credit hour MSc in three semesters full-time, or progress gradually by taking one credit-bearing micro-credential certificate at a time based on your availability and professional commitments. These stackable certificates can then be accumulated toward the Postgraduate Diploma (20 credit hours) and ultimately the MSc award (30 credit hours).
If you are ready to lead the digital and global health revolution, we invite you to apply. You can find more details on our website or by contacting the Dubai Medical University College of Medicine.
Can I continue working while enrolled in the program?
Yes, the program is designed to be working-professional friendly:
Online components are scheduled in the evenings.
On-campus sessions are delivered at weekends.
Are scholarships or financial support options available?

Yes. The tuition fees for the MSc program are AED 100,000 for the full three-semester program. A 5% VAT applies (AED 5,000), bringing the total fee to AED 105,000 inclusive of VAT. To support the inaugural intake, a 25% tuition discount will be offered to students admitted to the first cohort, total would be AED 75,000 + AED 3,750 VAT = AED 78,750 inclusive of VAT.

The Postgraduate Diploma tuition fee is AED 60,000; however, students admitted to the first cohort will benefit from a reduced fee of AED 50,000, a 5% VAT (AED 2,500) will apply, resulting in a total fee of AED 52,500 inclusive of VAT.

The tuition fee for each Credit-Bearing Micro-Credential (CBMC) certificate is AED 15,000. A 5% VAT applies (AED 750), bringing the total fee to AED 15,750 inclusive of VAT. Please note that no tuition discount currently applies to the CBMC certificates.
When will the program start, and what are the application deadlines?

The program is scheduled to launch in the Fall Semester of the 2026–2027 academic year, with classes expected to commence in August 2026. Information regarding application opening dates, deadlines, and admission timelines will be announced through Dubai Medical University’s official website and admission channels.

Dubai Medical University (DMU) embodies the visionary legacy of the late H.E. Saeed Ahmed Lootah, a trailblazer in UAE education. The inception of Dubai Medical College for Girls in 1986 and Dubai Pharmacy College in 1992 attests to his commitment. Recognizing the importance of interdisciplinary collaboration and a holistic approach to healthcare education, the transformative merger of these established institutions, along with the addition of the College of Nursing in 2024, marks a significant milestone—the birth of Dubai Medical University. Since its establishment, DMU has continued to expand its academic offerings with the recent addition of the College of Health Sciences in 2026.

This evolution aims to establish a comprehensive healthcare education institution offering a diverse range of programs, from undergraduate to postgraduate degrees, across various healthcare fields. The establishment of DMU not only elevates educational standards but also provides students with a more inclusive and well-rounded learning experience, impacting the healthcare industry in Dubai and the UAE positively.

Multiple Mini Interview (MMI) – MD Program Admissions

The Multiple Mini Interview (MMI) is a structured interview process used in admissions to the MD program to assess professional and personal competencies essential for success in medical training and professional practice.

Unlike traditional interviews, the MMI consists of a series of short, focused stations designed to evaluate candidates across a range of scenarios. This approach helps ensure fairness, reliability, and objectivity by minimizing individual interviewer bias and allowing candidates multiple opportunities to demonstrate their strengths.
The MMI assesses the following competencies:
These competencies complement academic performance and reflect attributes expected of future physicians.
The MMI includes a combination of live interaction stations and written response stations.
All stations are assessed independently by trained examiners using standardized scoring rubrics.
Clear instructions are provided at each station.
No prior clinical knowledge is required.
Scenarios and tasks are appropriate to the level of a medical student or trainee.
Assessment focuses on reasoning, communication, and professional attributes.
For written stations, language and grammar are not assessed separately.

Dubai Medical University College of Medicine proudly stands as the first private medical college in the UAE to award a degree in Medicine and Surgery. Founded through the vision of Haj Saeed Lootah, the College was established on strong Islamic values to provide women in the UAE the opportunity to pursue medical education locally, empowering them to serve their nation with confidence and purpose.

Today, the College advances that legacy through innovative, future-focused programs delivered within a values-driven academic environment. Our curricula are continuously reviewed and refined in alignment with the best global practices in medical education, ensuring academic excellence and societal relevance.

Beginning Fall 2025, the College introduces a restructured, competency-based 2+4 Doctor of Medicine (MD) curriculum. The first two years focus on general education, followed by two years of integrated biomedical sciences and two years of immersive clinical clerkships.

In addition to the six-year MD track, a Graduate Entry MD (4-year) pathway enables qualified degree holders to enter directly into advanced stages of the program. Uniquely, graduates of health sciences programs may join the MD in Year 3, reinforcing academic mobility and interdisciplinary progression. Both pathways are globally benchmarked and designed to cultivate clinically competent, ethically grounded physicians.

The BBMS program is a forward-looking degree aligned with the UAE Professional Qualification Framework, preparing graduates for national and international certifications. It equips students with scientific expertise, critical thinking, and innovation skills essential for leadership in laboratory medicine, biomedical research, and the broader healthcare and life sciences sectors. The program opens diverse pathways into clinical practice, research, postgraduate education, and healthcare leadership.

To strengthen academic leadership in healthcare, the College offers postgraduate qualifications in Health Professions Education, including a Postgraduate Diploma, and Master’s degree. These programs empower healthcare professionals to excel as educators, curriculum designers, and academic leaders in an evolving global health landscape.

Beyond academics, the College nurtures a vibrant student life. Through an active student union and a wide range of scientific, cultural, social, community, and sports initiatives, students build lifelong professional bonds and meaningful community engagement.
We invite aspiring young women to join College of Medicine, Dubai Medical University, where tradition meets innovation, and education becomes a pathway to service, leadership, and impact.

The General Education curriculum at Dubai Medical University aims to:

by fostering lifelong learning, intellectual curiosity, self-awareness, professionalism, and the transferable knowledge, skills, and values required for academic success, professional practice, and responsible citizenship.
by integrating knowledge from the humanities, social sciences, natural sciences, technology, and health sciences to support holistic, evidence-informed, and patient-centered healthcare.

by developing effective communication, critical thinking, quantitative reasoning, digital literacy, teamwork, ethical responsibility, and cultural awareness for lifelong personal and professional development.
by encouraging creativity, entrepreneurship, sustainability, and leadership to address contemporary healthcare challenges and contribute positively to local and global communities.
Upon successful completion of the General Education curriculum at Dubai Medical University, students will be able to:
Demonstrate clear, responsible, and professional written and oral communication skills appropriate for diverse audiences and contexts.
Apply critical thinking skills to evaluate evidence, analyze complex issues, and make informed decisions.
Use contemporary digital technologies, computing tools, and information resources effectively for academic, professional, and personal purposes.
Demonstrate awareness of local (UAE) and global issues while exhibiting cultural sensitivity, inclusivity, and appreciation of diversity.
Demonstrate ethical behavior, integrity, accountability, and social responsibility in academic, personal, and professional contexts.
Apply principles of innovation, entrepreneurship, and sustainability to develop creative solutions that contribute to professional growth and address societal challenges.
Collaborate effectively in individual and team settings, demonstrating respect, inclusivity, and productive engagement with individuals from diverse cultures, disciplines, and backgrounds.
Apply mathematical and quantitative reasoning skills to interpret, analyze, and communicate quantitative information for informed decision-making.

This course is designed to help undergraduate students at Dubai Medical University enhance the academic reading and writing skills essential for success in their university studies. The course focuses on developing abilities in reading comprehension, summarization, paraphrasing, essay structure, and research-oriented writing. Students will engage with both general and academic texts and learn how to produce various genres of academic writing, including expository essays. Students will gain skills in critical reading, constructing well-organized paragraphs and essays, and using appropriate academic language in their written work.

The course covers a wide range of topics related to the United Arab Emirates in the contemporary era, focusing on introducing the student to the theoretical and empirical aspects that define political life in the country. It also sheds light on the country’s position in the international arena and its performance in global competitiveness. The course also delves into Emirati society's values, essential heritage, and efforts to develop the Emirati people and foster their contributions to the betterment of the society, emphasizing their crucial role in shaping the country's future. The course also highlights significant achievements in vital national fields, showcasing the UAE’s efforts in furthering human competencies and striving towards the future, the goals of empowering women and achieving development, and the unique features of the UAE’s cultural and literary richness. The course also addresses issues of priority for prudent leadership, including meeting food security requirements and ensuring community safety and prosperity through efforts to enhance community health, improve wellbeing practices, the country’s pioneering pursuits in environmental sustainability, and efforts to achieve technical development and employ its achievements in various fields.

The course “Entrepreneurship, Innovation and Sustainability” has been allotted 3 credit hours which are to be covered over 15 weeks. This course focuses on the concepts and the interconnection between entrepreneurial thinking, innovation and sustainable development. The course is designed in 3 parts to explain the main principles of entrepreneurial process; to link them with concept of innovation and to engage in sustainable development to affect positive societal change. This course will teach students how to think like an entrepreneur and provide the models, tools and frameworks to further develop business or ideas. For future healthcare professionals, this course ensures the ability of decision making to be balanced between professional, ethical approaches on one side, and finance and business on the other side.

The course Technology in Health has been allotted 2 credit hours which will be covered over 15 weeks. Before commencing the course, the students should have basic computer skills and English proficiency. This course is designed to provide students with basic information about digital learning and health informatics, and to equip them with the essential skills required as healthcare professionals. The course covers digital innovations and the role of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in healthcare education and training. It also explores the evolution of digital learning education and the web and debates their role in contemporary healthcare education and training. It explores the breadth of technology application, current and emerging trends and showcases both local and international e-health practice and research. The course will stimulate the students to evaluate how e-health can improve the coordination and efficiency of healthcare, and what the barriers might be.

Principles of Psychology is a foundational course designed for first-year undergraduate students across disciplines. Spanning 14 weeks, the course introduces the scientific study of behavior and mental processes through core areas such as biological bases of behavior, sensation and perception, states of consciousness, learning and memory, cognition, intelligence, motivation, and emotion. Students will explore developmental milestones, personality theories, stress and health psychology, and gain an understanding of psychological disorders through the DSM-5 framework. Emphasis is placed on evidence-based treatment approaches, including psychotherapy and biomedical interventions. The course also integrates elements of social psychology, including group dynamics and clinician-patient interactions. Through lectures, discussions, and applied case studies, students will develop foundational psychological literacy and learn to apply psychological principles to health, wellbeing, and everyday life.

This course develops the foundational knowledge and practical communication skills required for effective interprofessional collaboration in healthcare and academic settings. Students explore the principles and processes of human communication while developing competencies in verbal, non-verbal, written, digital, interpersonal, and group communication. Emphasis is placed on communication competence, active listening, self-awareness, intercultural communication, teamwork, conflict management, ethical communication, and professional presentations. Through interactive learning activities, students develop effective communication skills to support collaborative and professional practice across health professions.

Medicine is not only a biological science; it is also shaped by social, cultural, ethical, and human factors. Humanities in Medicine introduces students at the beginning of their medical education to the human and social dimensions of medicine and the complex interactions among patients, healthcare professionals, families, communities, and healthcare systems.

Through literature, narrative medicine, ethics, visual arts, film, patient stories, and reflective practice, students explore the lived experiences of health, illness, suffering, healing, and mortality. The course encourages students to understand patients as individuals with unique stories, values, identities, and cultural contexts rather than as clinical cases alone.

The course provides an early foundation for competencies that will continue to develop throughout the six-year MD program, including ethical reasoning, empathy, professionalism, communication, collaboration, reflective practice, and professional identity formation. When Breath Becomes Air by Paul Kalanithi serves as the principal narrative text, complemented by ethical case discussions, selected films, visual arts, and experiential learning activities.

Students will begin developing an e-portfolio to document their reflections, learning experiences, personal development, and emerging professional identity throughout their medical journey. By integrating scientific knowledge with humanistic understanding, the course promotes patient-centered care, compassion, ethical awareness, professionalism, and respect for human dignity.

Learning in the Modern World is a two-credit general education course that introduces BPharm/PharmD students to the skills, habits, and mindsets that will support them throughout their academic and professional journey. Rather than aiming for mastery of any single discipline, the course gives students a broad, practical orientation to topics they are unlikely to encounter explicitly elsewhere in the curriculum: understanding themselves as learners, using evidence-based study strategies, evaluating information critically, engaging responsibly with AI tools, collaborating and communicating with peers and faculty, and learning through experience and community engagement. By the end of the course, students will have a foundational map of the learning, collaboration, and professional-growth skills they will continue developing throughout their pharmacy education and beyond.

A vision statement is a future-based statement that is a declaration of the Program’s long-term goals. Long-term goals may include a patient improvement benefit. Usually, Programs include the values that will help them to achieve their goal.

A mission statement is a present-based statement of purpose for the Program, the Program’s reason for existing. The reason usually includes a description of their learners, Program impact, and methods used to make the change (simulation, research, assessment, etc.). The mission statement should guide the actions of the Program and related decision-making.

Dubai Medical University (DMU) is fundamentally committed to fostering an inclusive, diverse, and equitable community for all its stakeholders. The university’s mission is dedicated to driving a quality culture and structure that ensures diversity, equality & inclusion. DMU actively promotes the UAE values of tolerance and acceptance across the campus environment through various initiatives and awareness campaigns.

The institutional commitment ensures that all employees and stakeholders adhere to core values of fairness and equitable treatment, inclusiveness, collegiality, respect, integrity, honesty, and ethical behavior.
DMU ensures that all students have the right to a safe and inclusive learning environment. This commitment is formalized through specific departments dedicated to student welfare and success.

The mandate for promoting diversity and inclusion among students belongs to the Deanship of Student Affairs (DSA) and the elected Student Council. Deanship of Student Affairs (DSA) Role: The DSA is specifically tasked with promoting diversity and inclusion initiatives and creating a welcoming and inclusive campus environment for students from all backgrounds. Student Voice and Representation: The elected Student Council, which operates under the coordination of the DSA, plays a key role in supporting this mission by actively promoting Diversity and Inclusion and fostering an environment that provides equal opportunities for all students.
DMU operates as an equal opportunity institution that will not distinguish between race, religion, or gender when admitting and formulating an offer to an applicant.
Students are legally entitled to respect in an educational environment which is free from threat, harassment, abuse, or discrimination.
DMU strictly prohibits discrimination, non-tolerance, and hate speech.
Any student misconduct that compromises academic integrity or community standards, including harassment or bullying, is subject to disciplinary action.
DMU operates as an inclusive community committed to addressing the educational needs of its Students of Determination (SOD) on campus.
Students requiring support must submit an official medical report of their diagnosis.
Appropriate accommodation is provided on campus depending on the students’ educational needs to support them in achieving their goals.
The DSA provides holistic support focusing on students’ physical, mental and emotional wellbeing. This support is aimed at responding to the needs of the comprehensive student population.
Diversity and Equality for Faculty and Staff
DMU is committed to maintaining transparency, fairness, and equality across all employment and administrative practices.

The responsibility for ensuring diversity, equity, and inclusion for faculty and staff belongs to the Human Resources (HR) Unit. DMU’s comprehensive Policy on Disability, Equity, Diversity, and Inclusion applies to all job applicants and employees (including faculty, staff, researchers, and professional staff). The purpose of this HR-led policy is to create an environment that is inclusive, diverse, and equitable for all employees.
